name: csharp-dev-tools
description: Enhanced development tools for C# and .NET in VS Code

languageModelTools.name: csharp-dev-tools_build_dotnet
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Build a .NET solution or project using C# Dev Tools. It uses the user's selected build configuration, target framework for project targets, terminal preference, NuGet credential handling, and build diagnostics. Use this instead of a generic terminal build whenever the user asks to build .NET code. It returns only a concise success message or the same structured build-error summary shown by C# Dev Tools. Do not use it to run tests.

target_path.description: Optional absolute path to a .sln, .slnx, or .csproj file. Omit it only when exactly one solution is loaded.

languageModelTools.name: csharp-dev-tools_test_dotnet
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Run .NET tests through the C# Dev Tools test runner at project, namespace, class, or individual-test scope. It respects the user's selected build configuration, target framework, detected test runner mode, .runsettings file, integrated build behavior, and NuGet credential handling. Use this instead of a generic terminal test command when a test project path is known. Set test_scope to project to run all tests, namespace for one namespace, class for one fully qualified test class, or test for one fully qualified test method. test_name is required for every scope except project. It returns only a concise success message, structured test failures, or a structured build-error summary when the required build fails. Do not use it for non-test projects.

project_path.description: Absolute path to the .csproj test project whose tests should run.

test_scope.description: The test granularity: project runs all project tests; namespace, class, and test select a specific target.

test_name.description: Required when test_scope is namespace, class, or test. Use the fully qualified namespace, class, or test method name respectively.

languageModelTools.name: csharp-dev-tools_add_ef_migration
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Create an Entity Framework Core migration using the same workflow as C# Dev Tools' Add Entity Framework Migration Run button. It builds the selected startup or migrations project first, applies NuGet credentials, runs dotnet ef migrations add with --no-build, saves the migration preferences, opens the created migration file, and returns a concise result. Use it when the user explicitly asks to create an EF Core migration. migrations_project_path is the project containing the DbContext and generated migrations. startup_project_path is optional but should be supplied when the application startup project differs. db_context_class and migrations_folder are optional and map directly to the dialog fields.

migration_name.description: Required migration class name, for example InitialCreate or AddUserTable.

migrations_project_path.description: Required absolute path to the .csproj that contains the DbContext and where migrations are generated.

startup_project_path.description: Optional absolute path to the startup .csproj used to load application configuration and connection strings.

db_context_class.description: Optional DbContext class name for solutions with multiple DbContexts.

migrations_folder.description: Optional migrations output directory relative to the migrations project, for example Migrations or Data/Migrations.

languageModelTools.name: csharp-dev-tools_create_diagram
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Create a local editable Excalidraw diagram or iteratively update an existing one in the C# Dev Tools editor. Use this for architecture, flow, sequence, deployment, data-flow, class, and infrastructure diagrams. For a new diagram pass diagram_name; it is stored under .vscodecsdt/Diagrams and opened immediately. To modify a diagram returned by an earlier call, pass its absolute diagram_path and operation 'merge', reuse stable element ids to replace elements, and use delete_element_ids to remove elements. The open canvas updates live after every call so the user can watch the work. Build a clear left-to-right or top-to-bottom layout with at least 60px gaps, short labels, consistent colors, and arrows after their endpoint shapes. Prefer 220x100 nodes, section headings as text, and a restrained palette. Keep connectors away from unrelated nodes and avoid crossing labels or other connectors. Use icon elements with icon_name for recognizable Azure resources or common Tabler symbols; bundled SVGs are matched and embedded into the file. For an icon set icon_source to azure or tabler when the intended family matters. Arrows bind to shape edges through start_element_id and end_element_id. Use operation 'replace' only when intentionally rebuilding the whole canvas. The tool returns an automatic quality report and, on supported VS Code versions, a rendered PNG. You MUST inspect that result for clipped text, overlaps, awkward spacing, connector crossings, visual hierarchy, and overall polish. If any issue remains, call this same tool again with the returned diagram_path and operation 'merge'. Do not claim completion until the automatic report is clean and the rendered diagram is visually satisfactory.

diagram_name.description: Name for a new workspace diagram. Omit when diagram_path identifies an existing diagram.

diagram_path.description: Absolute path to an existing .excalidraw file to update. Reuse the path returned by an earlier call.

operation.description: replace rebuilds the scene from the supplied elements; merge preserves other elements and upserts supplied stable ids. Defaults to replace for new files and merge for existing files.

background_color.description: Optional canvas background as a hex color.

delete_element_ids.description: Stable ids to remove during a merge. Connected arrows and generated labels are cleaned up automatically.

elements.description: Elements to create or upsert. Shapes with text get centered, wrapped labels automatically.

id.description: Required stable id using letters, numbers, hyphens, or underscores. Reuse it to update this element later.

text.description: Label for a shape or content for a text element.

start_element_id.description: For arrows or lines, stable id of the source shape.

end_element_id.description: For arrows or lines, stable id of the destination shape.

points.description: Optional points relative to x/y for an unbound arrow or line.

icon_name.description: Search phrase for a bundled Azure or Tabler SVG, for example app service, sql database, service bus, user, or cloud.

languageModelTools.name: csharp-dev-tools_create_debug_runner
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Scaffold a C# Dev Tools runner that reproduces a bug and write a provided C# body into its Run() method. A runner is a lightweight entry point that wires up the target project's dependency-injection container and lets you invoke code directly under the debugger without starting the full application. Use this as the first step of an agentic debugging flow: given a description or stack trace, generate a minimal reproduction body. If a runner project does not yet exist for the source project it is created automatically. source_project_path is the absolute path to the .csproj to reproduce against. runner_name is a PascalCase C# class name. runner_body contains the C# statements placed inside 'public async Task Run()'. services is the list of dependencies to inject through the runner constructor - ALWAYS pass the services your runner_body needs (prefer interfaces such as IOrderService) so the code compiles immediately without a fix-up loop; each injected service is resolved from the project's DI container and exposed as a field with the given (or derived camelCase) name that runner_body can reference directly (e.g. orderService). usings is an optional list of additional namespaces. Returns the created runner file path and class name. After creating, set breakpoints and call debug_run_runner.

source_project_path.description: Absolute path to the .csproj to reproduce the bug against.

runner_name.description: PascalCase C# class name for the runner, for example OrderBugRunner.

runner_body.description: C# statements to place inside 'public async Task Run()'. Use these to reproduce the bug. Reference any injected services by their field name (e.g. orderService).

services.description: Dependencies to inject through the runner constructor. Pass every service the runner_body uses so it compiles on the first try. Prefer interface types that are registered in the project's DI container.

type.description: The C# service type to inject, preferably an interface, for example IOrderService.

name.description: Optional field/parameter name for the service. Defaults to a camelCase name derived from the type (leading interface 'I' dropped), e.g. IOrderService becomes orderService.

usings.description: Optional additional namespaces to import (e.g. MyApp.Services). Each entry may be a bare namespace or a full 'using X;' statement. Include the namespaces of any injected service types.

languageModelTools.name: csharp-dev-tools_debug_set_breakpoints
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Add source breakpoints in C# files before running the debugger. Supports conditional breakpoints (condition), hit-count conditions (hitCondition) and logpoints (logMessage). Use this to mark the critical locations you want to inspect while diagnosing a bug. Set replace_existing to true to first remove breakpoints previously added by this tool. Returns the breakpoints that were set. Breakpoints may show as unverified until a debug session is running.

condition.description: Optional C# boolean expression; the breakpoint only triggers when it is true.

logMessage.description: Optional logpoint message; when set, execution logs instead of stopping. Use {expr} to interpolate expressions.

replace_existing.description: When true, remove breakpoints previously added by this tool before adding the new ones.

languageModelTools.name: csharp-dev-tools_debug_run_runner
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Build and launch a runner under the .NET debugger and wait until it hits a breakpoint, terminates, or times out. runner_file_path is the absolute path returned by create_debug_runner. method_name optionally targets a single method (defaults to Run). timeout_ms bounds how long to wait for the first stop (default 30000). Returns a stop summary: status 'stopped' with the top stack frame and thread id, 'terminated' when the program finished without stopping (includes console output), or 'timeout'. After a stop, use debug_get_state, debug_evaluate, debug_step and debug_continue to investigate, then debug_stop to end the session.

runner_file_path.description: Absolute path to the runner .cs file to debug.

method_name.description: Optional runner method to invoke. Defaults to Run.

timeout_ms.description: Maximum time in milliseconds to wait for the first stop. Default 30000.

languageModelTools.name: csharp-dev-tools_debug_get_state
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Inspect the current paused state of the managed debug session. Returns the call stack for the stopped thread and, unless include_variables is false, the local variables of the selected frame. thread_id defaults to the last stopped thread. frame_index selects a stack frame (0 = top). Use this after a breakpoint stop to collect the data needed to diagnose a bug.

thread_id.description: Optional stopped thread id. Defaults to the last stopped thread.

frame_index.description: Optional 0-based stack frame index. Defaults to 0 (top frame).

include_variables.description: Whether to include local variables for the selected frame. Defaults to true.

languageModelTools.name: csharp-dev-tools_debug_evaluate
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Evaluate a C# expression in the context of a paused debug frame and return its value and type. Use this to probe object state, call simple property getters, or check conditions while stopped at a breakpoint. frame_index selects the stack frame (0 = top); thread_id defaults to the last stopped thread. Requires an active managed debug session that is paused.

frame_index.description: Optional 0-based stack frame index to evaluate in. Defaults to 0 (top frame).

thread_id.description: Optional stopped thread id. Defaults to the last stopped thread.

languageModelTools.name: csharp-dev-tools_debug_continue
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Resume the paused debug session and wait for the next breakpoint, termination, or timeout. thread_id defaults to the last stopped thread. timeout_ms bounds the wait (default 30000). Returns the same stop summary shape as debug_run_runner. Use this to advance between breakpoints while investigating.

thread_id.description: Optional thread id to continue. Defaults to the last stopped thread.

timeout_ms.description: Maximum time in milliseconds to wait for the next stop. Default 30000.

languageModelTools.name: csharp-dev-tools_debug_step
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Perform a single debugger step and wait for the resulting stop. step_type selects 'over' (step over the current line), 'in' (step into a call), or 'out' (step out of the current method). thread_id defaults to the last stopped thread. timeout_ms bounds the wait (default 30000). Returns the same stop summary shape as debug_run_runner. Use this to trace execution line by line while diagnosing a bug.

step_type.description: The kind of step to perform.

thread_id.description: Optional stopped thread id. Defaults to the last stopped thread.

timeout_ms.description: Maximum time in milliseconds to wait for the next stop. Default 30000.

languageModelTools.name: csharp-dev-tools_debug_stop
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Stop the managed runner debug session and return the tail of its console output. Set remove_breakpoints to true to also remove the breakpoints previously added by debug_set_breakpoints. Call this when the investigation is complete, before or after applying a fix. If no session is active, returns status 'no_session'.

remove_breakpoints.description: When true, remove the breakpoints previously added by debug_set_breakpoints.

walkthroughs.title: C# Dev Tools
walkthroughs.description: Learn how to use all the enhanced C# features

steps.title: Solution Explorer
steps.description:
The enhanced Solution Explorer provides a familiar Visual Studio-like experience for .NET development in VS Code.

**Solution Structure:** View all projects, solution folders, references, and files
**Context Menu:** Access build operations, manage user secrets, NuGet management, and more
**File Management:** Create, move, and organize files directly in the Solution Explorer

[Open Solution Explorer](command:csharp-dev-tools.openSolutionViewer)

steps.title: Test Explorer
steps.description:
Run and debug your .NET tests directly from VS Code.

**Automatic discovery** of tests in your solution
**Run tests** individually, by group, or the entire solution
**View test results** and navigate directly to test failures

[Open Testing View](command:workbench.view.testing.focus)

steps.title: Advanced Search
steps.description:
Quickly find and navigate to C# types and symbols in your codebase.

Press **Alt+P** to open the search dialog
Search for **types** (classes, interfaces, enums, structs, records)
Find **members** using @methodName syntax
Search within specific types with TypeName@memberName syntax

[Open Advanced Search](command:csharp-dev-tools.advancedSearch)

steps.title: NuGet Package Management
steps.description:
Manage NuGet packages directly from the Solution Explorer.

**Open** the NuGet Manager by right-clicking on a project or using the button below
**Browse** for new packages to install
**Update** existing packages to newer versions
**Remove** packages you no longer need

The NuGet Manager will automatically detect your solution file.

[Open NuGet Manager](command:nugetManager.openPackageManager)

steps.title: Project Creation
steps.description:
Create new .NET projects directly from VS Code.

**Project Templates:** Access standard .NET project templates
**Solution Integration:** Automatically add new projects to your solution
**Configuration:** Set up project properties during creation

[Create New Project](command:solutionViewer.newProject)

steps.title: Quick Add
steps.description:
Quickly add new files, classes, and components to your project with Shift+F2.

**Fast File Creation:** Press Shift+F2 when focused on the Solution Explorer to instantly add new items
**Smart Templates:** Choose from C# classes, interfaces, enums, records, controllers, Razor pages, and more
**JSON to C# Conversion:** Paste JSON objects to automatically generate C# classes with proper attributes
**Context-Aware:** Automatically adds files to the correct project folder based on your selection
**No Menu Navigation:** Skip right-click menus and create files instantly

Try it now by selecting a project or folder in the Solution Explorer and pressing Shift+F2!

**New JSON Feature:** You can now paste JSON like `{"name":"John","age":30}Address.cs` to create C# classes!

[Open Solution Explorer](command:csharp-dev-tools.openSolutionViewer)

media.altText: Quick Add feature showing file creation dialog

steps.title: Editor Features
steps.description:
Take advantage of enhanced C# editing features:

**Type Inlay Hints:** See inferred types for var declarations
**Unused Symbol Highlighting:** Easily identify dead code
**Navigation Shortcuts:**
  Shift+Alt+L: Reveal current file in Solution Explorer

Toggle these features from the Command Palette or extension settings.

[Open Settings](command:workbench.action.openSettings?%22csharp-dev-tools%22)

media.altText: Editor features showing inlay hints and navigation

csharp-dev-tools.codeLens.enableReferenc.description: Show 'X references' code lens on types and members

csharp-dev-tools.codeLens.enableTypeInit.description: Show 'X initializations' code lens on types to find where they are instantiated

csharp-dev-tools.codeLens.enableMemberAs.description: Show 'X assignments' code lens on public properties and fields

csharp-dev-tools.inlayHints.enableTypeHi.description: Show inlay type hints for C# var declarations

csharp-dev-tools.inlayHints.enableParame.description: Show inlay parameter name hints for C# method calls

enumDescriptions: Launch in VS Code's integrated terminal
Launch in VS Code's internal console (Debug Console)
Launch in an external terminal window
csharp-dev-tools.debug.launchConsole.description: Controls where console applications are launched when debugging. Indicates which console the target program should be launched into. See https://aka.ms/VSCode-CS-LaunchJson-Console for more information.

csharp-dev-tools.debug.programArguments.description: Command line arguments to pass to the program when debugging or running. These arguments will be passed to the main method of programs.

csharp-dev-tools.debug.skipBuild.description: Skip building the project before debugging. When enabled, the debugger will launch the last built version of the project without rebuilding.

csharp-dev-tools.debug.enableWatch.description: Enable 'dotnet watch' during debugging. When enabled, uses 'dotnet watch run' to support live code changes. When disabled, uses standard 'dotnet run'.

csharp-dev-tools.debug.openOutputOnBuild.description: Automatically open the 'C# Dev Tools' output channel when building projects. When enabled, the output panel opens automatically to show build logs.

csharp-dev-tools.debug.runBuildInTermina.description: Run build commands in a VS Code terminal instead of the output channel. When enabled with 'Open Output on Build', the terminal will be focused automatically.

csharp-dev-tools.debug.offerToRunLastBui.description: When a build fails, offer to run the last successful build if previous build artifacts exist. Shows a modal dialog with the age of the last build.

csharp-dev-tools.debug.colorizeStatusBar.description: Apply custom colors to the Run and Debug buttons in the status bar. When enabled, the Run button is shown in green and the Debug button in red for better visual distinction.

csharp-dev-tools.debug.showJumpToLineLen.description: Show a 'Jump to Line' indicator on the current cursor line during debugging. Clicking it executes 'Set Next Statement' to move the execution point to that line.

enumDescriptions: Show as a CodeLens above the line
Show as grayed-out text at the end of the line
csharp-dev-tools.debug.jumpToLineIndicat.description: Controls how the 'Jump to Line' indicator is displayed during debugging.

enumDescriptions: Show the hint at the end of the line
Show the hint at the start of the line
csharp-dev-tools.debug.jumpToLineHintPos.description: Controls the position of the inline hint when using 'Inline Hint' indicator style.

csharp-dev-tools.build.configuration.description: Build configuration used when running, debugging, testing, or collecting coverage. Choose a project-defined configuration from the status bar.

csharp-dev-tools.build.targetFramework.description: Target framework used when running or debugging multi-targeted projects. Choose a project-defined target framework from the status bar.

enumDescriptions: Group tests by Project > Namespace > Class (default)
csharp-dev-tools.testing.groupBy.description: How to organize and group tests in Test Explorer. Change requires refreshing tests.

csharp-dev-tools.inlineDebugValues.enabl.description: Show variable values inline in the editor during debugging sessions. Values are displayed at the end of lines where variables are declared or used. Changed values are highlighted in a different color.

csharp-dev-tools.inlineDebugValues.showA.description: Show actual values for arrays and lists (e.g., [1, 2, 3]) instead of just the count (e.g., List<int> [3 items]). When disabled, only the type and count will be shown for better performance with large collections.

csharp-dev-tools.inlineDebugValues.maxAr.description: Maximum number of items to show when displaying array/list values inline. If the collection has more items, only the first N items will be shown with '...X more' indicator.

csharp-dev-tools.inlineDebugValues.showO.description: Show object properties inline as JSON-like format (e.g., { name: "John", age: 30 }) instead of just the type name. When disabled, only the type will be shown for better performance with complex objects.

csharp-dev-tools.inlineDebugValues.maxOb.description: Maximum number of object properties to show when displaying object values inline. If the object has more properties, only the first N properties will be shown with '...X more' indicator.

csharp-dev-tools.inlineDebugValues.maxNe.description: Maximum depth level for expanding nested objects. Level 1 shows only direct properties, level 2 shows properties of properties, etc. Higher values may impact performance with deeply nested objects.

csharp-dev-tools.inlineDebugValues.highl.description: Highlight changed variable values in a different color (red). When disabled, all debug values will use the same color regardless of whether they have changed.

csharp-dev-tools.highlights.xmlComments.description: Enable syntax highlighting for XML documentation comments (tags, attributes, and values)

csharp-dev-tools.highlights.controllerTe.description: Enable syntax highlighting for controller route templates (route parameters like {id} and tokens like [controller])

enumDescriptions: Highlight only template variables like {Name} with a single color (Rider-style)
Highlight template variables and arguments with multiple colors
csharp-dev-tools.highlights.stringTempla.description: Controls highlighting for logger string templates (e.g., LogInformation)

csharp-dev-tools.highlights.sqlHighlight.description: Enable syntax highlighting for raw SQL queries in C# string literals (SQL keywords and parameters like {0})

csharp-dev-tools.highlights.todoComments.description: Enable C# TODO comment highlighting added by C# Dev Tools

csharp-dev-tools.templates.useFileScoped.description: Use file-scoped namespaces in templates for .NET 6+ projects. When enabled, templates will use file-scoped namespace syntax (namespace MyNamespace;) instead of traditional block namespaces for .NET 6+ projects. For older .NET versions, traditional namespaces will be used regardless of this setting.

csharp-dev-tools.templates.globalUsingsF.description: Preferred filename for Global Using files. This file will be created when you use the 'Add > Global usings' command or when moving using statements from other files.

csharp-dev-tools.quickAdd.jsonToCsharp.u.description: Convert property names to PascalCase when generating C# classes from JSON.
Generate fields instead of properties when creating C# classes from JSON.
Use nullable reference types (?) for properties in generated C# classes.

csharp-dev-tools.quickAdd.jsonToCsharp.a.description: Add JsonProperty attributes from Newtonsoft.Json to generated properties.

csharp-dev-tools.quickAdd.jsonToCsharp.n.description: Add NullValueHandling.Ignore to JsonProperty attributes when using nullable types.

csharp-dev-tools.quickAdd.jsonToCsharp.u.description: Use JsonPropertyName attributes from System.Text.Json instead of Newtonsoft.Json.

csharp-dev-tools.quickAdd.jsonToCsharp.g.description: Generate immutable classes with get-only properties.

csharp-dev-tools.quickAdd.jsonToCsharp.u.description: Generate C# record types instead of classes.
Use IReadOnlyList<T> instead of List<T> for array properties.

csharp-dev-tools.quickAdd.jsonToCsharp.g.description: Generate separate .cs files for each class when converting complex JSON objects.

enumDescriptions: Apply semantic colors only to current workspace
csharp-dev-tools.semanticColors.mode.description: Controls where C# semantic token colors are applied. Global applies to all workspaces, workspace applies only to current workspace, off disables the feature.

csharp-dev-tools.semanticColors.interfac.description: Custom color for C# interface tokens. Leave empty to use theme-aware defaults (dark: #b8ce82, light: #2e7d32).

csharp-dev-tools.semanticColors.enumColo.description: Custom color for C# enum tokens. Leave empty to use theme-aware defaults (dark: #b8ce82, light: #7b1fa2).

csharp-dev-tools.semanticColors.namespac.description: Custom color for C# namespace tokens. Leave empty to use theme-aware defaults (dark: #cccccc, light: #616161).

csharp-dev-tools.semanticColors.structCo.description: Custom color for C# struct tokens. Leave empty to use theme-aware defaults (dark: #86C691, light: #0277bd).

csharp-dev-tools.semanticColors.inactive.description: Custom color for C# code excluded by an inactive preprocessor branch. Leave empty to use a theme-aware gray.

csharp-dev-tools.pullRequestManager.grou.description: Group pull requests by status (open, closed, merged)

csharp-dev-tools.nuget.persistNuGetCrede.description: When enabled, NuGet credentials injected into nuget.config files will persist after dotnet operations complete. By default (false), credentials are automatically removed after operations complete for security. Enable this setting if you want credentials to remain in the configuration files permanently.

csharp-dev-tools.nuget.showVersionDecora.description: Show version status indicators (✅/🆕) next to PackageReference elements in .csproj files. ✅ indicates the package is up to date, 🆕 indicates a newer version is available.

csharp-dev-tools.nuget.enableCodeActions.description: Enable code actions (quick fixes) for updating package versions in .csproj files. When the cursor is on a PackageReference line, shows all available versions with markers for (latest) and (current).

csharp-dev-tools.nuget.enableCompletions.description: Enable IntelliSense completions for NuGet package names and versions in .csproj files. Provides autocomplete suggestions when typing <PackageReference Include=" or Version=".

csharp-dev-tools.testGeneration.defaultM.description: Default language model to use for test generation. Leave empty to use the first available model. You can specify a model ID (e.g., 'copilot-gpt-4') or partial name.

csharp-dev-tools.playwright.showBrowser.description: Show browser window when running Playwright tests. When enabled, tests run in headed mode (visible browser), when disabled tests run in headless mode (faster, no UI).

csharp-dev-tools.playwright.enableDebugg.description: Enable Playwright debugger when running tests. When enabled, tests will pause at each step and open the Playwright inspector for debugging.

csharp-dev-tools.playwright.slowMode.description: Enable slow mode for Playwright tests. When enabled, adds a 500ms delay between actions to make test execution easier to follow visually.

csharp-dev-tools.playwright.overrideRunS.description: Override detected .runsettings files with custom Playwright settings. When enabled, uses the Playwright-specific settings instead of any detected .runsettings files.

csharp-dev-tools.excalidraw.autoSaveDela.description: Delay in milliseconds after the last change before auto-saving. Lower values save more frequently but may impact performance.

csharp-dev-tools.roslyn.workspacePropert.description: Additional MSBuild properties to pass to the workspace (e.g. Configuration=Debug).

csharp-dev-tools.roslyn.showItemsFromUni.description: Determines if items from unimported namespaces are shown in completion lists.

csharp-dev-tools.roslyn.targetTypedCompl.description: Determines if target-typed completion is enabled.

csharp-dev-tools.roslyn.triggerCompletio.description: Trigger completion when a space is typed.

csharp-dev-tools.roslyn.showCompletionTy.description: Show return/property types as inline hints in the autocomplete list. Disabling may improve completion performance in large projects.

csharp-dev-tools.roslyn.addCompletionMet.description: Add parentheses to method completions and trigger signature help when needed.

csharp-dev-tools.roslyn.skipUnrecognized.description: Determines if unrecognized projects are skipped when projects are opened.

csharp-dev-tools.roslyn.loadMetadataForR.description: Determines if metadata from existing output assemblies is loaded instead of opening referenced projects. Significantly speeds up workspace loading for solutions that have been built.

csharp-dev-tools.roslyn.restoreProjectsB.description: Determines if projects are restored before they are loaded.

scripts.vscode:prepublish: npm run build-speedscope && npm run build-webviews && npm run package
scripts.compile:full: cd webviews && npm run build && cd .. && webpack
scripts.build-server: dotnet publish ../csharp-dev-tools-lsp/server/CsharpDevTools.Roslyn.Server/CsharpDevTools.Roslyn.Server.csproj -c Release -p:AssetsPath=%cd%/extension/bin/ && dotnet publish ../csharp-dev-tools-lsp/server/CsharpDevTools.Debugging.Mono/CsharpDevTools.Debugging.Mono.csproj -c Release -p:AssetsPath=%cd%/extension/bin/
scripts.build-webviews: cd webviews && npm ci && npm run build
scripts.build-speedscope: cd external/speedscope && npm install && npm run build-release -- --outdir "dist" --protocol file
scripts.pretest: npm run compile-tests && npm run compile && npm run lint
